_meta.indication: Indicated in combination with other antiemetic agents in adults for the prevention of delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of emetogenic cancer chemotherapy, including, but not limited to, highly emetogenic chemotherapy

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel group, controlled study; VARUBI regimen (VARUBI, granisetron and dexamethasone) vs control (placebo, granisetron and dexamethasone)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults receiving a cisplatin-based highly emetogenic chemotherapy regimen (cisplatin >60 mg/m2)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete Response (no vomiting, retching or rescue medication) in the delayed phase
pivotal_trials.n: 532 randomized (VARUBI N=266, control N=266); 526 evaluated for efficacy
pivotal_trials.result: Delayed-phase CR 72.7% VARUBI vs 58.4% control; p<0.001; treatment difference 14.3 (95% CI 6.3, 22.4)

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel group, controlled study; VARUBI regimen (VARUBI, granisetron and dexamethasone) vs control (placebo, granisetron and dexamethasone)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults receiving a cisplatin-based highly emetogenic chemotherapy regimen (cisplatin >60 mg/m2)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete Response in the delayed phase
pivotal_trials.n: 555 randomized (VARUBI N=278, control N=277); 544 evaluated for efficacy
pivotal_trials.result: Delayed-phase CR 70.1% VARUBI vs 61.9% control; p=0.043; treatment difference 8.2 (95% CI 0.3, 16.1)

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel group, controlled study in moderately emetogenic chemotherapy; VARUBI regimen vs control
pivotal_trials.population: Adults receiving moderately emetogenic chemotherapy, with at least 50% receiving an anthracycline plus cyclophosphamide combination
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete Response in the delayed phase
pivotal_trials.n: 1369 randomized (VARUBI N=684, control N=685); 1332 evaluated for efficacy
pivotal_trials.result: Delayed-phase CR 71.3% VARUBI (N=666) vs 61.6% control (N=666); p<0.001; treatment difference 9.8 (95% CI 4.7, 14.8)

key_safety: In Cycle 1, adverse reactions in ~7% of VARUBI patients vs ~6% control. HEC (cisplatin): neutropenia (9% vs 8%), hiccups (5% vs 4%), abdominal pain (3% vs 2%). MEC/AC: decreased appetite (9% vs 7%), neutropenia (7% vs 6%), dizziness (6% vs 4%)
target_moa: Rolapitant is a selective and competitive antagonist of human substance P/NK1 receptors; NK-1 inhibition is important for prevention of nausea and vomiting during the delayed phase
modality: Small molecule (oral NK-1 receptor antagonist; new molecular entity, molecular weight 554.95)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held to discuss this NDA; there were no significant public health questions requiring the committee's input

summary.text: Standard full approval of an oral NK-1 inhibitor (new molecular entity) for prevention of delayed CINV; NDA submitted September 5, 2014 with a PDUFA goal date of September 5, 2015 (12-month standard review) and approved on the first cycle without an advisory committee meeting. Efficacy was based on three phase 3 trials (two HEC, one MEC). No special expedited designations were stated.

citations.quote: The applicant has submitted an NDA for an oral NK-1 inhibitor, rolapitant 90 mg, a new molecular entity intended to prevent chemotherapy induced nausea and vomiting (CINV).

Date of Submission	September 5, 2014
PDUFA Goal Date	September 5, 2015
There was no advisory committee meeting held to discuss this NDA.
